home: Open Ad Studio. Switch Default Brand and an owned Brand Kit; inspect recent projects and the template/brief actions.
Recent projects follow the selected brand. Creatives are inside their own project. Starting-point clicks only open setup; no project is silently saved.
brief: Create a test project or open an owned project. Edit objective, audience, message, direction and CTA; save and reopen.
Saved fields remain consistent with Project Details; failed saves do not start generation.
templates: Browse templates, change aspect ratio and open a template.
Thumbnails, selected format and template identity stay consistent.
template: Choose a standard layout in Default Brand, review project setup and save explicitly. For a Brand Kit, inspect approved saved Brand Templates and reuse one in a compatible owned project.
No project is created by clicking Home Use template. Missing model/source permissions or unavailable template services are explicit; no orphan project is created by a failed creative request.
assets: Review the selected kit and product assets in the project.
Only authorized assets are offered; original photographs and logo roles are identifiable.
progress: During an owner-authorized request, inspect pending, completion and failure states.
Status represents the actual request; no simulated completion or automatic paid retry.
concepts: Save a distinctive brief and request concepts. Inspect provider labeling; change direction and compare.
Copy and art direction reflect the saved brief; heuristic output is never labeled live AI.
detail: Open a concept and inspect headline, rationale, CTA, asset plan and format.
The full selected concept is shown and can continue into creative creation.
compare: Select two concepts and compare message, audience and visual direction.
Different concepts remain identifiable; selection is retained after returning.
preview: Open a saved creative and compare its text, product image and logo with the editor.
Preview shows the selected saved creative without broken media or invented branding.
edit: Edit headline, CTA, product placement and logo. Exercise undo/redo, save and reopen.
Layers remain editable and saved changes survive reopening in the existing Canvas.
variations: Create a native variation, change its text or layout and reopen both versions.
The original is preserved; deterministic variations are labeled honestly.
workspace: Create multiple static creatives from different templates in one test project; reopen it.
Every creative appears in the same project; names, bindings and versions persist.
formats: Choose square, portrait, story and landscape formats for a saved creative.
Dimensions match the chosen format and required source layers remain present.
export: Export a saved creative in each offered image format. Open downloaded files.
Files decode, have expected dimensions, and match preview text, image and placement.
performance: Inspect availability of connected campaign metrics. Do not treat demonstration metrics as real.
Real data has provenance; unavailable integrations are explicitly identified.
director: Review campaign context, request a plan and compare recommendations with your brief.
Planning, review and comparison capabilities are clear; incomplete orchestration is disclosed.
brand-intelligence: Inspect recommendations, rationale, review and approval controls where available.
No brand or creative is silently changed; missing campaign intelligence stays identified.
product-lab: Inspect original product binding, mask readiness and review gates.
A rejected mask stays rejected; geometry checks do not imply creative-quality approval.
visual-lab: With the owner-approved runtime ready, generate one ad background using an approved original product.
The request reaches the configured Google provider; source product, printed branding and editable text remain protected.
composition: Inspect product, background, logo and text layers; move each independently.
The result uses the existing AdSceneGraph/Canvas and keeps deterministic brand layers separate.
advanced-canvas: Exercise available alignment, layering and inspector controls. Record missing prototype tools.
Existing tools work without a second editor; advanced parity gaps are explicit.
variation-lab: After owner authorization, request a meaningfully different background and a natural-language refinement.
Provider-backed results retain source bindings and versions; requests do not retry automatically.
adaptation: Adapt a saved creative to a second placement; inspect crop, text wrapping and safe areas.
The source is retained and the new format remains editable; clipping is reported.
campaign-manager: Inspect project creatives, names, selected concept and saved campaign context.
Owned project records remain linked; organization actions do not silently duplicate assets.
motion-studio: Inspect storyboard, image sequence, Veo and Sound Design availability without starting video generation.
Implemented controls and missing orchestration are distinguished; no video runs automatically.
delivery: Inspect actual publishing destinations, permissions and confirmation flow.
Unsupported channels are labeled; no campaign is published by opening this screen.
dna-quality: Inspect brand consistency, evidence and human approval requirements.
Numerical scores do not replace visual review or automatically approve assets.
preflight: Run the available preflight with required assets present and missing.
Ownership, source, capability and approval blockers are explicit; no generation or credit transaction occurs.
brand-info: Open the existing ZOE kit in the new layout. Review name, description, industry, website and signature product.
The same Brand Kit ID is used; saved optional fields and asset associations are preserved.
brand-category: Review category/niche, change only in a disposable kit and inspect dependent approvals.
Canonical categories work and a change requires re-review instead of silently approving identity.
brand-goals: Review goals, personality, tone, audience and detailed copy fields.
Existing values remain editable and persist through the same Brand Kit.
brand-assets: Check existing logos/product images, candidate selection and library search. Attach an authorized test image if desired.
Existing assets are visible; explicit attachment preserves original content and does not grant generation approval.
brand-analysis: Inspect the analysis gate. Only after owner approval, review a provider proposal before applying.
No automatic paid call; proposal changes and approval requirements are understandable.
brand-guidelines: Review photography, lighting, composition, prohibited claims and freeform guidance.
Structured and freeform guidance survive save/reopen; approval is explicit.
brand-overview: Review palette, typography, uploaded assets, approvals and saved versions.
Preview uses the real kit and labels sample layouts; identity approval is not inferred from uploads.
brand-templates: Select a Brand Kit on Home and in a project; inspect its actual saved-template library, then review/approve/save a recipe when the runtime is enabled.

Only this kit’s saved approved recipes are offered for reuse. Generic catalog overlays and illustrative Example Brief references are labeled separately. Record HTTP 503 as blocked until local activation is approved.
brand-template-detail: Open a native template, review format and required product/logo bindings, then use it in a project.
Unsupported capabilities and missing assets block execution rather than fabricate replacements.
category-studio: Inspect category/niche-specific templates and guidance across available categories.
Production availability is distinguished from the five-category prototype.
brand-manager: Open Brand Kits. Inspect palette/product covers, search, export, new-kit entry and existing-kit links.
Real records look like distinct brands; the new editor is the single editing experience.
